idiom_name: async methods returning promises + a serializing promise chain
implementation_notes: A JavaScript realm runs one thread, so an object's methods already execute on the realm's thread and the pattern's own-thread-of-control half cannot be created in-process; what remains is the future half. An active-object-like class therefore exposes async methods returning Promise<T>, serializes state transitions by chaining onto a tail promise (or an async queue), and reaches for a Web Worker or worker_threads only when real parallelism is needed, exchanging messages rather than sharing state. The classic proxy/queue/scheduler roles are replaced by the event loop's task queue plus async/await.
pitfalls: A promise chain serializes only what is chained: an async method that mutates state without awaiting the chain interleaves at its first await.
CPU-heavy servant work blocks the single thread shared by every object; move it to a Worker and copy data instead of sharing closured state.
Unawaited rejections become unhandled rejections (fatal under Node's default policy); every method's promise must be observed or handled.
